title: The graph engine runs this repository's own real workload
description: Conformance runs on a synthetic fixture. Before claiming the engine is finished, run it against the real 29 KB PlanSpec this repository actually produces, end to end.

successCriteria.description: A graph run completes against the real committed workload corpus, not the synthetic conformance fixture.
Every channel stays within its declared cap for that workload, measured and reported rather than assumed.
The run's node coverage and verdict are recorded, and any node that does NOT execute on a real workload is named with its reason.
The result is committed as evidence — a real-workload record a later flip decision can be taken against.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, and the golden gate passing at or above its replay floor.

stopConditions: The real workload exceeds a channel cap or a superstep ceiling — that is the finding, and it is worth more than a passing run. Report the measured number rather than raising the cap reflexively.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: spec-20260812-pge-real-workload-errors already built the corpus and sized the caps to it (sprint 3 of that spec, graphVersion 1.3.0); reuse that corpus rather than inventing one. That spec's sprint 1 also established the measurement approach — follow it, and report numbers rather than a pass/fail. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees. Verify on a CLEAN checkout, not just the working tree: this repo has twice been green locally and red in CI because uncommitted state was carrying the result.
evaluatorNotes: The point is measurement, not a green tick. Check real numbers were reported for every channel, and that a node failing to execute on the real workload was named rather than averaged away. Run the suite as `npx vitest run --exclude '**/.claude/worktrees/**' --exclude '**/node_modules/**'` — a bare run picks up nested worktrees.
